════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Enterprise: Parker-Hannifin Corp (PH), US Industrial — diversified motion

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE & HISTORICAL PATTERN
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 1.5-1. Similar Enterprise Base Rate Inquiry

• Probability of achieving a 30%+ adjusted segment margin in industrial

  anchors caution)
• Probability of cyclical industrial demand continuing expansion 3 years
  from a current acceleration point: ~50–60%

Step 1.5-2. Deviation of Current Analysis from Base Rate
My base case assumes ~10–12% adjusted EPS CAGR for 5 years (FY26–30) and
30% segment margin by FY31. This is ABOVE the mature-industrial base
rate. Justification (3+ company-specific reasons):
1. Parker's Win Strategy execution track record: adjusted segment
   margin expanded from ~19% (FY19) to 27.3% (FY26) — company-specific
   operational discipline
2. Aerospace backlog at record $8.5B and total backlog $12.8B: visibility
   that partially secures future revenue
3. Portfolio mix shift toward longer-cycle/resilient end markets
   (aerospace, defense, semi, data center) reduces cyclicality and
   supports higher margin plateau
4. Management has already hit the previous 27% target three years early,
   providing credibility for the 30% FY31 target
5. Order momentum: Q4 FY26 orders +19% overall, Industrial NA +16%,
   International +24%, Aero +18%

Step 1.5-3. Base Rate Shock Check
• Probability of success here (>30% margin, >10% EPS CAGR) is ~50–60% in
  my base case vs. ~25–35% base rate. This is ~1.7x — within the
  "require additional evidence" band. I have elevated evidence from the

  probability to 2.0x. Conclusion: base case is at the high edge of

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY ASSESSMENT (BUFFETT + LYNCH)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 2-1. Business Understanding
• PH designs and manufactures motion-control systems (hydraulics,
  pneumatics, electromechanical, filtration, sealing) for industrial
  and aerospace customers.
• Diversified Industrial (NA + International) sells to off-highway,
  factory automation, energy, truck, and process industries;
  Aerospace Systems sells to commercial and defense OEMs plus aftermarket.
• The business is a classic owner-operator, distribution-led industrial
  with strong aftermarket/FMRO (fleet maintenance, repair, overhaul)
  exposure.
• Understandability: HIGH — clear earnings drivers, segment disclosure,
  asset-heavy but transparent economics.

Step 2-2. Moat Assessment (0–3 each; 7 types)
• Intangible assets (brand, know-how): 2 (Parker is a strong brand in
  motion control; proprietary engineering)
• Switching costs: 3 (flight-critical parts certification; industrial
  hydraulic systems integrated into customer designs)
• Network effects: 1 (distribution/service network is extensive, but not
  classic two-sided network)
• Cost advantage: 1 (global scale, but not lowest-cost producer in every
  line)
• Economies of scale: 2 (broad distribution, purchasing, engineering R&D
  leverage)
• Regulatory barriers: 2 (aerospace certifications, defense security
  clearance)
• Data moat: 1 (condition monitoring aftermarket data, but nascent)
  TOTAL: 12/21 → WIDE MOAT (lower end)
• Moat direction: STABLE-to-WIDENING. Aerospace backlog record;
  industrial recovery; aftermarket attach rate/monitoring data building.
  No single threat visible that would narrow the moat in the next 3 years.

Step 2-3. Lynch Classification
• PH is a STALWART/CYCLICAL hybrid: long-term growth mid-single-digit,
  cyclical fluctuations; Aerospace segment adds secular growth.
• Checkpoints: dividend increases 70 consecutive years; FCF conversion
  >90%; management reducing cyclicality through mix shift; PEG
  unattractive at T0 (see Section 3).

Step 2-4. Financial Strength Scorecard
[All annual figures from SEC companyfacts, [Actual], FY ends June 30]
• Revenue growth (3-yr CAGR FY23–FY26): from $19.065B to $21.499B →
  +4.1% CAGR. 5-yr CAGR: +8.4% [Actual, pack]
• Operating margin FY26: $5.068B/$21.499B = 23.6%; 12-yr median: 16.4%
  [Actual]
• Adjusted segment operating margin FY26: 27.3% [Company]
• EPS (diluted, GAAP): FY26 $28.48; adjusted $32.31 [Company]
• ROE: FY26 net income $3.649B / avg equity (($13.691+$15.413)/2 =
  $14.552B) = 25.1% [Arithmetic, [Actual-based]]
• ROIC (approximate, GAAP): NOPAT ~$4.6B / avg invested capital
  (equity + debt − cash) ~$25B → ~18–19% [Estimate]
• FCF: FY26 $3.905B (OCF $4.364B − capex $0.459B) [Actual]; FCF
  conversion = $3.905B/$3.649B = 107% of net income [Arithmetic]
• Net debt (my definition): LT debt $7.472B + current portion $1.754B
  + short-term borrowings $1.000B + finance leases $0.092B + operating
  leases $0.213B − cash $0.501B − ST investments $0 (not held 2026,
  [Unconfirmed]) ≈ $10.03B [Arithmetic, assumption on overlap]
• Net debt / EBITDA: $10.03B / ~$6.0B (EBITDA ≈ OI $5.068B + D&A $0.937B)
  ≈ 1.7x [Estimate]
• Interest coverage: OI $5.068B / interest (est $450–500M) ≈ 10–11x
  [Estimate]
• Balance-sheet classification: GOOD — investment grade, manageable
  leverage, high FCF conversion. No pension or inventory red flags
  (inventory / revenue ~14.7%, reasonable [Arithmetic]).

Step 2-5. Capital Allocation Scorecard (0–3 each, total 15)
1. Buyback efficiency: 2 — consistent repurchases; FY26 returned ~$2B;
   shares down ~1.6% y/y and 3-yr CAGR −1.1% [Actual, pack]. Not
   aggressively counter-cyclical, but disciplined; shares ~5% below avg
   price of last years.
2. M&A track record: 2 — Meggitt acquisition (2022) appears to be
   delivering synergies; CIRCOR aerospace ($2.55B) and Filtration Group
   (price unconfirmed) pending; record not unblemished, but above base
   rate.
3. Capex efficiency: 3 — capex low (0.5% of sales), high incremental
   ROIC; this is an asset-light assembly/manufacturing model now.
4. Rationality of mix: 3 — M&A in adjacent flight-critical/filtration;
   buybacks funded by FCF; dividend increase 11%.
5. Guidance accuracy: 3 — FY26 initial guidance raised multiple times;
   Q4 beat; credibility high.
   TOTAL: 13/15. Insider ownership: not disclosed in pack; large insider
   sells not flagged → no adjustment. Base capital-allocation score: 13.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 2.5-1. R&D Capitalization
• Parker does not disclose R&D as a separate line in the pack; most
  industrial companies expense product engineering inside SG&A (PH SG&A
  includes substantial engineering). I estimate R&D = $0.9–1.1B,
  ~4.5–5% of revenue, based on industrial comparables [Assumption —
  no PH-specific disclosure retrieved].
• Amortization (5-yr, straight-line) on R&D = ~20% of capitalized pool
  per year. If capitalized R&D pool = 5× $1.0B = $5.0B, amortization =
  $1.0B/yr. Since expensed R&D ≈ amortization ≈ $1.0B, the adjustment
  to operating income is approximately neutral. Net effect on
  operating margin: +~0 to +0.3%. [Estimate]
• Adjusted Op. margin: ~23.6–23.9% vs GAAP 23.6%. Immaterial.

Step 2.5-2. SBC Proper Treatment
• SBC FY26: $0.179B [Actual, pack] — ~0.8% of revenue. Deduct from FCF:
  Owner FCF FY26 = $3.905B − $0.179B = $3.726B. [Arithmetic]
• This is the cash-flow base I use for valuation (FCF after SBC).

Step 2.5-3. Operating Lease Capitalization
• Operating leases: $0.213B (FY26) [Actual]. Capitalizing at 7x →
  ~$1.5B off-balance-sheet debt [Estimate]. Total adjusted net debt:
  ~$11.5B (vs $10.0B). EV +~$0.5–1.5B. Impact on WACC/EV minor but
  included in net-debt line for EV math.

Step 2.5-4. Brand/Data Asset Estimation
• Brand: Parker has strong industrial brand but not a consumer brand;
  no Interbrand value available. Contribution embedded in pricing power/
  gross margin. [Unconfirmed — not valued separately to avoid double
  count.]
• Data: aftermarket condition monitoring/data services growing but not
  separable in pack; no numerical valuation attempted beyond
  recognizing the optionality. [Unconfirmed]

Step 2.5-5. Adjusted ROIC Calculation
• Adjusted NOPAT ≈ $5.068B × (1 − 22% est. tax) + R&D-neutral adj ≈
  $3.95B [Estimate; tax rate assumed 22%, [Assumption]]
• Adjusted invested capital = equity $15.413B + total debt (incl.
  leases) ~$10.5B − cash $0.501B + capitalized R&D pool $5.0B ≈
  $30.4B [Arithmetic/Estimate]
• Adjusted ROIC ≈ $3.95B/$30.4B ≈ 13.0% [Estimate]
• GAAP ROIC ≈ 18–19% [Estimate]; the GAAP figure overstates ROIC because
  it ignores R&D as a capital asset. 5%+ gap explained by R&D
  capitalization and low-capex model.
• Note: Adjusted ROIC 13% > WACC ~8.5% — still value-creative, but
  less striking than GAAP ROIC suggests. [Estimate]

Step 2.5-6. Owner Earnings (Buffett Style)
• Owner earnings FY26 = Net income $3.649B + D&A $0.937B − maintenance
  capex (≈$0.50B, [Estimate — D&A exceeds actual capex, so maintenance
  capex is bounded by capex $0.459B; use $0.459B as total and ~$0.35B
  as maintenance]) − ΔWC (FY26 +$0.468B use of cash) − SBC $0.179B
  ≈ $3.649+0.937−0.459−0.468−0.179 = $3.48B [Arithmetic]
• This is the conservative distributable-cash base: ~2.8% yield on
  market cap. Valuation uses FCF after SBC, not owner earnings, to
  capture growth capex.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 3. VALUATION ENGINE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 0-1/0-2. Enterprise Classification & Engine Selection
• Archetype: B (Quality Compounder) blended with C (Cyclical) —
  PH has a cyclical industrial base but has transformed toward
  aerospace/defense/long-cycle exposure. I call it B/C hybrid with
  Aerospace as the quality-compound engine and Industrial as cyclical.
• Valuation engine: Engine 1 (Traditional DCF + Multiples) as PRIMARY,
  with Engine 2 (cycle-adjusted) as a cross-check on the Industrial
  segment. Engine 3 (hybrid) not applicable (not product-platform).
• Why Engine 1: PH is free-cash-flow positive, has stable historical
  margins, clear segments, and a defensible long-term margin target.
  A DCF anchored on actual FY26 FCF and management's disclosed targets
  is the most appropriate primary.
• Cross-check valuation: 12-yr median EV/EBITDA, peer P/E, and
  cycle-adjusted normalized EPS.

Step 3-1. DCF Assumptions & Explicit Forecast (FY27–FY31, then terminal)
All [Assumption] unless footnoted. Sources: FY27 guidance [Actual,
company]; long-term targets [Actual, company].

Revenue ($B):
• FY26 actual: $21.499
• FY27: 6.5% growth (midpoint 5.5–8.5% reported (organic), FX −0.5%,
  prior acquisitions +0.5%) → $22.90 [Guidance midpoint]
• FY28: +5.0% (industrial recovery ongoing; aero mid-teens offset by
  slower industrial; management 4–6% organic target)
  → $24.05
• FY29: +5.0% → $25.25
• FY30: +4.5% → $26.39
• FY31: +4.0% (management 4–6% organic target lower end; base slows as
  Aero aftermarket growth normalizes) → $27.45
• FY32+ terminal: 3.5% nominal (long-run nominal GDP + pricing)

Segment Adjusted Operating Margin [Company-adjusted basis]:
• FY26 actual: 27.3% [Actual]
• FY27: 27.7% midpoint (guidance 27.5–27.9%) [Actual/Estimate]
• FY28: 28.2% (industrial recovery + aero mix)
• FY29: 28.7%
• FY30: 29.3%
• FY31: 30.0% (management target) [Actual target]
• Terminal: 30.0% — this is the critical assumption. 30% is
  significantly above the 27.3% achieved; it is the HIGH end of
  historical industrial margin range. I keep it because: (1) management
  has pre-announced it; (2) mix shift to aerospace; (3) Win Strategy
  execution has a proven record. But in the bear case, I step it down
  to 27–28%. [Assumption — see scenario section]

Operating income (adj. basis):
• FY27: $22.90 × 27.7% = $6.34B
• FY28: $24.05 × 28.2% = $6.78B
• FY29: $25.25 × 28.7% = $7.25B
• FY30: $26.39 × 29.3% = $7.73B
• FY31: $27.45 × 30.0% = $8.24B
• Tax rate: 22% (effective on adjusted basis; FY26 GAAP effective tax
  rate not directly given; assumed 22%, [Assumption])
• NOPAT:
  FY27: $4.95B; FY28: $5.29B; FY29: $5.66B; FY30: $6.03B; FY31: $6.43B
• D&A: FY27: $1.00B, growing 3%/yr → FY31 $1.13B [Estimate — capex/D&A
  ratio sustained]
• Capex: $0.50B FY27, growing 4%/yr → FY31 $0.59B [company-guided
  long-term FCF margin 17%, implies low capex requirement]
• ΔWC: FY27 $0.35B use, FY28 $0.30B use, FY29 $0.25B use, FY30 $0.20B,
  FY31 $0.20B (easing as growth normalizes) [Assumption]
• SBC: $0.19B growing at 5% → FY31 $0.23B [Assumption]
• FCF after SBC = NOPAT + D&A − Capex − ΔWC − SBC:
  FY27: $4.95+1.00−0.50−0.35−0.19 = $4.91B
  FY28: $5.29+1.03−0.52−0.30−0.20 = $5.30B
  FY29: $5.66+1.06−0.54−0.25−0.21 = $5.72B
  FY30: $6.03+1.09−0.56−0.20−0.22 = $6.14B
  FY31: $6.43+1.13−0.59−0.20−0.23 = $6.54B
• Note: FCF > net income throughout, consistent with the asset-light
  transformation and negative working-capital intensity of this model.

Discount Rate:
• Risk-free: 4.67% (10Y UST) [Actual, FRED]
• Equity risk premium: 4.5% (long-run historical, [Assumption])
• Beta: 1.13 (vendor, window unstated) [Estimate]
• Cost of equity = 4.67% + 1.13 × 4.5% = 9.76% [Arithmetic]
• Cost of debt: 5.2% (A-rated industrial, [Estimate]);
  after-tax 4.06%
• Weights: E = market cap $125.4B; D = $10.5B; E/V = 92.3%, D/V=7.7%
• WACC = 0.923 × 9.76% + 0.077 × 4.06% = 9.0% + 0.3% ≈ 9.3%
  → I use 9.3% (rounded). [Arithmetic/Estimate]
  Sensitivity: WACC 8.3–10.3% band → see Tornado.

Terminal value:
• Terminal growth: 3.0% (long-run nominal GDP, conservative vs 3.5%
  revenue terminal assumption)
• Terminal FCF = FY31 FCF × (1+3%) = $6.74B
• Terminal value at end-FY31 = $6.74B / (9.3% − 3.0%) = $107.0B
• PV of explicit FCFs (discounting mid-year convention):
  DF factors @ 9.3% (mid): FY27 0.956, FY28 0.875, FY29 0.801,
  FY30 0.733, FY31 0.671
  PV FCFs = $4.69 + $4.64 + $4.58 + $4.50 + $4.39 = $22.80B
• PV of terminal value = $107.0B × 0.671 = $71.8B
• Enterprise value = $94.6B
• Less: net debt (my definition incl. leases and ST investments at 0)
  $10.0B; less pension/other [none identified]
• Equity value = $84.6B
• Wait — this is far below T0 market cap $125.4B. Let me re-check.

[Recalculation check]
• The terminal multiple implied: EV/EBITDA at FY31 = $107B / (OI $8.24B
  + D&A $1.13B ≈ $9.37B) ≈ 11.4x — reasonable.
• The issue: 9.3% WACC with a modest terminal growth, applied to
  mid-single-digit-growth cash flows, simply does not justify $125B
  today unless the market assumes either (a) much higher near-term
  growth, (b) margin expansion beyond 30%, or (c) a much lower discount
  rate (~7%).
• Reverse DCF check:
  At $125.4B equity + $10.0B net debt = $135.4B EV.
  With WACC 9.3%, terminal growth 3%, the market requires FY31
  FCF ≈ $135.4B × (0.093 − 0.03) / (some growth path)…
  Actually, simpler framing: The market is capitalizing $6.5–7.0B FY31
  FCF at ~10–11x, or is using a 7.5–8.0% WACC (bullish).
  My 9.3% WACC produces IV ≈ $1,020 (before the recalculation the
  $84.6B equity value divided by 128.1M shares = $660; that used
  terminal FCF at FY31 and a 3% terminal rate.)
  Let me re-examine: which WACC/terminal assumptions would the market be
  using? EV $135.4B = PV of FCFs + PV(TV).
  If FCFs follow my path, PV(FCFs)=$22.8B, so PV(TV)=$112.6B required.
  TV at end FY31 then = $112.6B/0.671 = $167.8B.
  That implies Terminal FCF = $167.8B × (0.093−0.03) = $10.57B, i.e.,
  FCF margin 38% of FY31 revenue — far above management's 17% FCF
  margin target. Or the market is using WACC ~7.5–8%.

Conclusion: T0 price embeds either an 8% WACC (macro goldilocks) or a
much richer margin story than guidance. This is the core expectation gap.

• I therefore present a RANGE of intrinsic values:

(1) Conservative (my primary):
WACC 9.3%, terminal growth 3.0%, terminal FCF margin 23.8% (FY31 FCF/
revenue = $6.54B/$27.45B = 23.8% — already above the 17% target because
the DCF captures WC release and low capex; assume it stays 23.8%).
Equity value ≈ $84.6B / 128.1M = $660/share.

(2) Base (market-realistic):
WACC 8.5% (justified only if rates fall to ~3.5–4.0% 10Y + ERP 4.5%),
terminal growth 3.25%, FY31 FCF $6.54B. PV(FCFs) at 8.5% mid-year:
DF: FY27 0.960, FY28 0.885, FY29 0.816, FY30 0.752, FY31 0.693
PV = $4.71 + $4.69 + $4.67 + $4.62 + $4.53 = $23.2B
TV = $6.54×1.0325/(0.085−0.0325) = $6.75/0.0525 = $128.6B
PV(TV) = $128.6×0.693 = $89.1B
EV = $112.3B; Equity = $102.3B; Per share = $799.

(3) Bull (market's apparent):
